title: Golimowski et al. (2006): HST/ACS Multiband Coronagraphic Imaging of the Debris Disk around Beta Pictoris

evidence.locator: Section 2.2: HST programme 9987, ACS/HRC behind the 1.8 arcsecond occulting spot in F435W, F606W and F814W at two rolls, with alpha Pic (A7IV) as the reference; synthetic flux ratios F_alpha/F_beta of 1.65, 1.75 and 1.90 in F435W, F606W and F814W from Synphot, assuming V of 3.27 and 3.86, uncertain by 2% in each band; the two stars' positions differ by about 0.8 pixel

Section 2.2 and its footnote on calibrated surface brightnesses: Vega magnitudes of beta Pic from Synphot, F435W 4.05, F606W 3.81, F814W 3.68, with zero-point errors under 2% (Sirianni et al. 2005); the residuals of the PSF subtraction preclude accurate photometry within 1.5 arcseconds (about 30 au) of the star and along the occulting finger
Section 3.3.1 and Figure 17: the F606W/F435W and F814W/F435W flux ratios of the disc relative to the star are nonuniform and asymmetric about both projected axes
